old_title: Transfer news LIVE: Alvarez to Arsenal latest, Liverpool sign Barcola
new_title: Transfer deadline day LIVE: Alvarez to Arsenal and Enzo to Man City latest
old_text:
A hectic end to the summer transfer window could be in store as Premier League clubs scramble to get deals done ahead of Tuesday night's deadline.
Cody Gakpo is set to leave Liverpool and join Manchester City in a shock move with Bradley Barcola's switch from Paris Saint-Germain now confirmed. If Gakpo departs, the Reds could sign another winger, with previous interest in Ismaila Sarr from Crystal Palace having moved on from Brighton's Yankuba Minteh.
Atletico Madrid remain steadfast on keeping Julian Alvarez or moving him to a club that is not Barcelona - and Arsenal could yet make a late push for the Argentina striker.
Manchester City remain in talks to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, who brought in Emiliano Martinez over the weekend to solve their goalkeeping question. If Fernandez does leave, Chelsea may target a new midfielder, with previous interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals below:
Bradley Barcola's first words as a Liverpool player
"It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy.
"It took a long time but I'm really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play.
"I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League - it's one of my biggest dreams in my life.
"It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term - that's why I signed a long contract - and I hope I can do it.
"I had the chance to play twice in this stadium and I saw the atmosphere and how the fans were behind the Liverpool players.
"When I knew about Liverpool's interest in me, I didn't ask questions and I knew it was a very big club for me."
Liverpool complete statement signing of Bradley Barcola from PSG
Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain in a marquee addition to Andoni Iraola's squad.
The French forward arrives on a five-year deal for an initial fee of £106m, which could rise to £123m.
The 23-year-old has been a Liverpool target throughout this summer, and desired a move to Merseyside even while attracting interest from other clubs.
Barcola continues Liverpool's heavy investment over the past two years, with Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz brought in for more than £100m last summer.
Capped 28 times by France, Barcola was part of the PSG side that won back-to-back Champions League crowns in 2025 and 2026, featuring off the bench in both finals.
Copa Independent: Transfer window special!
Have you listened to the latest episode of Copa Independent yet? Our crack team of football writers dug deep into all the moving and shaking of this summer's wild transfer window, and looked at what it all might mean for the Premier League this season. It's available wherever you get your podcasts - or right here....
DONE DEAL! Daniel Munoz reunites with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest
A switch of Premier League clubs for Daniel Munoz, a favourite of Oliver Glasner now back with the manager after leaving Crystal Palace for Nottingham Forest.
"I'm really excited because I can see so much talent, Forest is a team with great players, great qualities and great skills on the pitch, I can't wait to get out there so I can help my new teammates and I think that we're going to do great things.
"The first thing is that this is a winning club. I think that when this is the expectation, the mentality, both for the management and the technical team, and for the players, this makes it special."
Manchester City complete signing of £32m winger as spending spree continues
Allan Elias said it was surreal and the proudest moment of his life to join Manchester City after completing his £32m move to the FA Cup winners.
The uncapped Brazilian has signed a five-year deal with City, who could pay Palmeiras a further £2m in add-ons.
The 22-year-old becomes one of the replacements for Savinho and Omar Marmoush, who have gone to Tottenham in deals that could earn City up to £145m, and may be the first of two wingers recruited at the end of the transfer window.
Michael Carrick says Man Utd will 'wait and see' as transfer deadline looms
Michael Carrick admits Manchester United could be active before the transfer deadline and says Marcus Rashford feels like a new signing after the returning forward helped secure a 5-2 win against Ipswich.
Asked about potential transfer activity, United boss Carrick said: "It's always difficult to say, to be honest, when there's so little time left.
"I think the situation that we're in, I think the business that we've managed to do, I'm pleased with. I think we're a better group, a better squad, potentially a better team.
"Adding Marcus into that feels like a new signing, so in that respect we're quite happy.
"We're always open to it if there's something else to be able to add, so I wouldn't shut that down. But as it stands, we'll have to wait and see."
How a reinvented Kobbie Mainoo could yet prove Manchester United's midfield answer
Manchester United have spent a small fortune overhauling their midfield this summer - but might a solution have been at the club all along? Richard Jolly assesses the promise that Kobbie Mainoo showed against Ipswich.
West Ham sign Viking forward
West Ham have signed Norwegian winger Edvin Austbo on a four-year contract with a further one-year option.
The 21-year-old, who joins from Viking FK, scored six goals and added seven assists last season in their Eliteserien-winning campaign, and was also named the Eliteserien Young Player of the Year.
Austbo said: "Obviously, the ambitions of the club are big and it's also for me as a player. The talks I had with Nuno and Nils Koppen were amazing and I just felt from the start that this was a good match and that I really wanted to come here.
"I watched English football on TV when I was a little kid. Everyone in Norway knows West Ham. It's such a big club and a club that belongs on the highest level in England."
Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez replacement?
Widespread reports suggest that Chelsea have identified Lamine Camara of Monaco as a possible midfield target to replace Enzo Fernandez, should the Argentine leave. The Senegal international is just 22 but already has plenty of experience in Ligue 1 and internationally.
Juventus 'lead chase' for Nick Woltemade
The striker merry-go-round could spin at quite the pace before tomorrow's deadline. The Telegraph reports that Juventus want Newcastle's Nick Woltemade, though a number of clubs are keen on a player who could be available.
new_text:
Transfer deadline day has arrived with two of the biggest sagas of the summer still to be resolved: will Arsenal sign Julian Alvarez and could Enzo Fernandez be swapping Chelsea for Manchester City before tonight's 11pm deadline?
Premier League champions Arsenal have pursued Alvarez all window but are running out of time to submit an offer to Atletico Madrid, despite selling Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus to free up space for the 26-year-old forward. It means the Gunners could be left short in attack if they do not meet Atletico's €150m asking price and so have explored alternatives - though they have turned down a possible deal for Lyon's Malick Fofana, who may now join Sunderland.
Manchester City, meanwhile, will need to submit a bid that is higher than £120m to sign Fernandez from Chelsea and complete their midfield rebuild. Fernandez has been left out of Chelsea's last two squads and Xabi Alonso's side will not sell the Argentina international without a suitable replacement, with Monaco's Lamine Camara, Roma's Manu Kone and Bournemouth's Alex Scott all on their radar.
Manchester United have still not signed a left back, while Liverpool's business appears done after signing Bradley Barcola and rejecting Manchester City's approach for Cody Gakpo. City have agreed a £60m deal with Everton to buy Iliman Ndiaye. That could have an impact on Everton's pursuit of Richarlison, with Tottenham still wanting to sign a new forward too.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals below
DONE DEAL! Chelsea sign Italian wonderkid Ahanor
Chelsea have agreed a deal to sign Italian international Honest Ahanor from Serie A side Atalanta.
The 18-year-old will not join the Blues until 2027, however, meaning the Italian club will loan the player out this season.
One for the future, Chelsea have spent around £40m on the defender.
Wrexham sign ex-Forest and Burnley defender Joe Worrall
Wrexham have signed defender Joe Worrall from Burnley, bringing an end to a frustrating two-year spell at Turf Moor where he struggled for appearances.
The 29-year-old helped Nottingham Forest earn promotion to the top flight in 2021/22 and will be hoping to rediscover his form at Wrexham.
He has signed a two-year deal for an undisclosed fee.
He said: "Everything that Wrexham's about, I'm going to throw myself into it head-first and give my all for this badge."
Everton to sign Maitland-Niles
Everton's busy day continues.
The Toffees have agreed a deal with Lyon for Ainsley Maitland-Niles.
The 29-year-old can play at full-back and in midfield.
Man City agree £60m deal for Iliman Ndiaye as Everton's pursuit of Jack Grealish progresses
Man City turned to Ndiaye after an approach for Cody Gakpo was rebuffed by Liverpool.
Fernandez to City dependent on replacement
The Independent's Chief Football Writer, Miguel Delaney, says that Enzo Fernandez's move to Manchester City is dependent on whether Chelsea can secure a guaranteed replacement before the deadline today.
The two options on the table for the Blues are Lamine Camara and Manu Kone of Monaco and Roma respectively.
Chelsea would need a purchase guaranteed for at least one of the midfielders before sanctioning the sale of Fernandez to City.
The Blues have seen a bid for Camara rejected at £38.5m while they continue to pursue Kone.
Monaco reject Chelsea bid of Camara
Earlier we brought you news that Chelsea had submitted a bid for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara who is seen as a replacement for the probably departing Enzo Fernandez.
Now an update has been given by Sky Sports who say that the bid, believed to be £38.5m, has been rejected by the French club.
Chelsea are still in talks with Roma over a £52m deal for Manu Kone.
DONE DEAL! Villa sign Mbaye
Aston Villa have completed the signing of PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye.
The deal is reportedly worth around £47m for the 18-year-old winger.
Ipswich to sign Burnley's Flemming
This is a less flashy transfer story but Ipswich look on track to sign Zion Flemming from Burnley for around £17m on deadline day.
Flemming would bolster Ipswich's attacking line and Gary O'Neill has been in the market for a centre forward.
Flemming scored 11 goals for Burnley last season in the top-flight and will bring Premier League experience. He is travelling to Ipswich to complete a medical and the formalities.
What is does do is leave Burnley a bit short for their Championship campaign. The Clarets would have hoped to bounce straight back up but they've lost two and drawn one of their opening three matches and sit in the second division relegation zone.
Woltemade set for Newcastle exit
Nick Woltemade is set to leave Newcastle just one year after signing for a record £69m from Stuttgart.
The forward is flying to Turin to complete a medical at Juventus on deadline day ahead of a probable loan move.
The forward wanted to remain at Newcastle but isn't seen as crucial to Matthias Jaissle's plans and Juve are willing to stump up a £3.5m season-long loan fee.
Napoli, Borussia Dortmund and other Bundesliga clubs also wanted the 24-year-old on loan.
Arsenal cool interest in Malick Fofana
Arsenal have cooled their interest in Lyon's Malick Fofana, who has been a target for multiple clubs this summer, with Mikel Arteta not viewing the winger as worth the €60m fee the French club want.
But The Guardian reports the 21-year-old now looks set to join Sunderland for an initial £25m rising to £31m.
